title: personal-llm-experiment-mini-tracker-isaac-2026-q1
content:
Quick personal mini-sheet for tracking small inference experiments and knobs. Mostly notes + small table I update as I iterate.

Summary: trying small quantization + batching combos to find low-cost low-latency sweet spot for 13B-ish models on dedicated A10 pools. Tracking crude p50/p95 latencies, throughput, and rough cost per 1k tokens.

Table (CSV-like):
run_id,date,model,quantization,batch_size,seq_len_prompt,seq_len_completion,p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1k_tokens,notes
run-20260110-a,2026-01-10,Llama2-13B,float16,1,64,128,210,420,320,0.85,"baseline float16 single-stream; stable but p95 spikes when other jobs run"
run-20260112-b,2026-01-12,Llama2-13B,4bit-llm,1,64,128,260,560,410,0.45,"4-bit quant (LLM.int8-like) smaller memory, better throughput, tail worse on cold cache"
run-20260115-c,2026-01-15,Llama2-13B,4bit-llm,4,64,128,480,940,1200,0.12,"batching x4 improves throughput massively, p50 ~2x but tail gets worse. Good for high-throughput endpoints"
run-20260118-d,2026-01-18,Mistral-7B,float16,1,32,64,95,170,900,0.30,"7B much cheaper/fast; quality tradeoffs on long-form prompts noted"
run-20260120-e,2026-01-20,Redwood-Base-3B,8bit,8,32,64,140,300,4200,0.06,"8-bit + batching 8 = best cost/unit for short completions; watch memory fragmentation on long-lived workers"
run-20260201-f,2026-02-01,Llama2-13B,4bit-llm,2,64,256,330,670,700,0.25,"increasing completion length increases p95 nonlinearly; consider KV cache warming"

Notes / TODOs:
- Add a column for GPU util and memory used next pass (helps correlate tail latency spikes).
- Re-run key runs with identical background noise to get tighter p95 (right now infra variance ~10-15%).
- Test cache-enabled runs (prefix caching) to measure latency improvements for repeated prompts.
- Try dynamic batching policy in serving runtime (target latency 300ms p95) and record failure/retry rates.

Observations:
- For interactive workloads (latency SLO <= 300ms p95), float16 single-stream or small batching (<=2) on 13B is workable but expensive.
- For throughput-oriented endpoints (batching okay), 4-bit quant + larger batch sizes gives best cost per 1k tokens; need to watch p95 for tail cases.
- 3-7B models still great for many user-facing features; can often push to 8-bit and batch heavily.

Quick log of experiments details stash (where I keep raw outputs):
- local notebook: ~/projects/inference/exp-isaac/2026-q1/
- cloud logs: s3://redwood-inference-experiments/isaac/2026/q1/
- brief notes PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/234 (early perf tweaks)

Small checklist before I convert to a more formal doc:
- [ ] Add GPU-level metrics (util, mem, pci-e bandwidth)
- [ ] Standardize cost calc (include infra amortization + amortized model storage)
- [ ] Run 5 repeats for each config to get CI on p50/p95
- [ ] Draft short one-pager for team with recommended default profiles for interactive vs batch endpoints

End of mini-sheet.
